x: The Most High says: The Most Gracious, O people, by His mercy upon you, He taught you the Qur’an and bestowed that upon you, for He made you see with it what pleases your Lord and made you know what displeases Him, so that you may obey Him by following what pleases Him and by teaching you what He has commanded you to do and by avoiding what displeases Him. Thus, you may deserve His abundant reward and be saved from His painful punishment.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding this matter: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Uqaili told us: Abu al-Awam al-Ujali told us, on the authority of Qatada, that he said in his interpretation of The Most Gracious * Taught the Qur’an: It is a great blessing, by God.

x: , God Almighty says: He created Adam, who is man according to what some of them say.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
He created man
, he said: Man is Adam.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
He created man
. He said: Man is Adam, peace be upon him.

x: Others said: Rather, he meant all people, and he used the singular form in the wording to convey it on behalf of his kind, as was said: Indeed, mankind is in loss Al-Asr 2. Both statements are not far from being correct, as the apparent meaning of the words allows them both.
, God Almighty says: He taught man eloquence. Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the statement in this place.
Some of them said: It means the statement of what is permissible and what is forbidden.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He taught him eloquence
, meaning God taught him the eloquence of this world and the next, between what is lawful and what is unlawful, so that he might use this as evidence for His creation.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
He taught him eloquence
- the world and the hereafter - so that he could use that as evidence against him.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Marwan told us: Abu al-Awam told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
He taught him eloquence
, he said: He made clear to him good and evil, what he should do and what he should leave.

x: Others said: It means speech, meaning that God Almighty taught man eloquence.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
He taught him eloquence

, that eloquence means speech. The correct thing to say about this is: The meaning of this is that God taught man what he needs in matters of his religion and his worldly life, of what is permissible and what is forbidden, of livelihood, of speech, and other things that he needs, because God, may He be glorified and praised, did not specify in His report that He taught him some of the explanation without others, but rather He was general and said: He taught him explanation, so it is as He, may He be glorified and praised, is general.

x: The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
, the people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is that
the sun and the moon move by precise calculation
and have phases that they run and do not exceed.

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told us: Al-Faryabi told us: Israel told us: Samak bin Harb told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
, he said: They are sent by calculation and stations.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
. He said: They move according to number and calculation.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Malik:
m: h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
. He said: By calculation and stations.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
: meaning by calculation and a set time.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement,
h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
, he said: They move according to a calculation.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement,
h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation

, that time and age are calculated by them. Were it not for the day and the night and the sun and the moon, no one would know how to calculate anything. If it were all night, how would it be calculated, or all day, how would it be calculated?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Marwan told us: Abu al-Awam told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
. He said: By calculation and a set time.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they run according to a certain amount.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Abdullah bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Sahba’, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The sun and the moon move by precise calculation
, he said: They move according to a precise measure.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they revolve around the same pole of a mill.

c: Muhammad bin Khalaf Al-Asqalani told us: Muhammad bin Yusuf told us: Israel told us: Abu Yahya told us on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Muhammad bin Yusuf told us: Warqa’ told us on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, according to a calculation, he said: Like the calculation of a millstone.
b.via: Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding God’s statement, according to calculation, he said: Like the calculation of the millstone. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: Its meaning is: The sun and the moon move according to calculations and stations, because calculation is a noun from the saying of the speaker: I calculated it according to calculations and calculations, like their saying: I disbelieved in it disbelief and I forgave it forgiveness. It has been said: It is the plural of calculation, as is the plural of meteor. The Arab scholars differed about the nominative case of the sun and the moon.

x: Some of them said: They were raised according to calculation, meaning by calculation, and the predicate was implied. He said: I think, and God knows best, that he said: They run according to calculation. Some of those who rejected this statement among them said: This is wrong. According to calculation, the sun and the moon are raised according to calculation. He said: The explanation will come in this: The explanation taught him that the sun and the moon are according to calculation. He said: It is not deleted or implied except in an anomalous manner in speech.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the star in this place, although they agreed that the tree is what stands on a stem.
Some of them said: What is meant by the star in this place of plants is what springs from the earth that spreads out over it and is not on a stem, such as grass and the like.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,

m: regarding his statement,
h
And the star
, he said: The star is everything that has gone with the earth as a bed. He said: The Arabs call the thil a star.

m: h

. He said: The star is the plant of the earth.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan:
m: h
And the star
. He said: The star is the one who has no leg.

x: Others said: The star in this place means the star of the sky.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And the star
, he said: The star of the sky.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: His statement,

and the star
, means: the star of the sky.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the star and the tree prostrate
. He said: He only means the star.
b.via: Muammar on the authority of Qatada

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: something similar. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: What is meant by the star is what grows from the earth of plants, because of the tree’s connection to it, so its meaning would be: what stands on a stalk and what does not stand on a stalk prostrates to God, meaning: that all things of different forms from His creation prostrate to Him, which is more similar and more deserving of the meaning of speech than anything else. As for his saying and the tree, the tree is what has been described before. And what we said about that was said by the people of interpretation.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the trees prostrate
, he said: The tree is everything that stands on a stem.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: regarding his statement, and the trees, he said: The tree is everything that stands on a stem.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada
m: regarding his statement, and the trees, he said: The trees are the trees of the earth.

And the trees prostrate

. He said: The tree that has a stem. c: Ibn Hamid told us: Tamim bin Abdul-Mumin told us, on the authority of Zubarkan, on the authority of Abu Razin and Saeed,
m: h
And the star and the tree prostrate
. They said: Their shadow is their prostration.

m: h
And the star and the tree prostrate
means that nothing of His creation descended from the sky except that it worshipped Him willingly or unwillingly.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: and this is the statement of Qatada.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,

, he said: They prostrate in the morning and the evening. And it was said:
h

, so he repeated it, and it is report on the authority of Juma’in. Al-Farra’ claimed that when the Arabs combined two plurals of non-humans, such as the lote tree and the

And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,

x: That you do not transgress in the balance
, means that God Almighty says: That you do not wrong or reduce the weight.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
that you do not transgress in the balance

, be just, O son of Adam, as you would like to be treated justly, and fulfill your obligations as you would like to be fulfilled, for justice is the goodness of people. Ibn Abbas used to say: O group of Mawali, you have been entrusted with two matters by which those who came before you were destroyed: this measure and this weight.

c: Amr bin Abdul Hamid told us: Marwan bin Mu’aya told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Abu Al-Mughira, who said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say in the market of Medina: O group of Mawali, you have been afflicted with two matters that have destroyed two nations: the measure and the scale.

x: He said: Marwan told us on the authority of Mughira who said: Ibn Abbas saw a man weighing and he had become heavier, so he said: Keep your tongue in check, keep your tongue in check. Didn’t God say:
And establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance

, means: And establish the tongue of the scale in justice. And His statement, And do not deprive people of the balance, means that God Almighty says: And do not reduce the weight when you weigh for people or wrong them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Marwan told us: Abu al-Awam told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the heaven He raised and set up the balance * That you not transgress within the balance *
h
And establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance

. Qatada said: Ibn Abbas said: O group of Mawali, you have been entrusted with two matters by which those who came before you were destroyed. A man should fear God when he holds his scales, and a man should fear God when he holds his measure. A small amount will equal it, and it will not decrease it, but rather God will increase it, God willing.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance
, he said: He made it less if he reduced it, so he made it less, his loss is his decrease.

x: God Almighty says: And the earth He laid out for all creatures. And He spread out the earth for creation, who are all creatures. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali told us: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, for mankind, meaning: for creation.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas,

h
And the earth He has spread out for all creatures
, he said: Everything that has a soul.

m: regarding his statement,
h
And the earth He has spread out for all creatures
, he said: For the creation of the jinn and mankind.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, for mankind, he said: for creation.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us:
m: He said: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: For mankind he said: For creation.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement, He placed it for mankind, that mankind means creation.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Marwan told us: Abu al-Awam told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the earth He laid out for all creatures. He said: For creation.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: similarly.

x: Therein is fruit and palm trees having sheaths

, God Almighty says: There is fruit in the earth, and the ha and the alif in it are from the mention of the earth, and palm trees having sheaths, and sheaths: the plural of kam, which is that which is sheathed in.
The interpreters differed on the meaning of this.
Some of them said: It means the palm tree being covered with fibres.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us on the authority of Abu Raja’
m: who said: I asked Al-Hasan about his statement,
h
And the palm trees with sheaths
, and he said: A frond made of fibers that I tied around it.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thaur told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and al-Hasan:
m: The one with sleeves. Its sleeves: its fibers.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the palm trees with sheaths
means the fibres that are on them.

x: Others said: By the sleeves he means the remains.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Marwan told us: Abu al-Awam told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And the palm trees with sheaths
. He said: Their sheaths are their fronds.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of the statement is: The palm tree with clustered spadixes on its scabbard.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
And the palm trees with sheaths

, and it was said: Does it have the spadix? He said: Yes, and it is in a sheath of it until it bursts open from it. He said: And the grain is also in sheaths, and he recited, And whatever fruits emerge from their sheaths Fussilat 47. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God described the palm tree as having sleeves, and its fruit is covered in its fibers and its dates are covered in its husk. God did not specify the report about it as being covered in its fibers nor its dates being covered in its husk, but rather He generalized the report about it as having sleeves. The correct thing to say is: What is meant by that is the one with a palm leaf and it is covered with it, and the one with a date palm and it is covered in its skin, so it is general as the Most High, the Most Praised, is general.

x: And the grain with husks and basil

, God Almighty says: And in it is the grain, which is the grain of wheat and barley with leaves and straw: it is the husk, and it was narrated to me by Alqamah ibn Abdah: Watering the sins whose summer rain has bent down, whose slopes are covered with rain. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the grain with husks and basil
, meaning figs.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me, my uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And the grain with husks and basil
. He said: The husk is the green leaves of the crop whose heads have been cut off, and it is called husk when it dries up.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed:
m: h
And the grain with husks
means the grass from the crops.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, and the grain with the husks, and its husks are its straw.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Asf means straw.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And the grain with the husk. He said: The grain is wheat and barley, and the husk is the straw.

m: regarding his statement,
h
And the grain with husks and basil
, he said: The grain is the first thing to grow.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Lahsan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
And the grain with husks and basil
, he said: The husk is the leaf of everything. He said: When a crop is cut, it is called a husk, and every leaf is a husk.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Yunus bin Muhammad told us: Abdul Wahid told us: Abu Rawq Atiyah bin Al-Harith told us:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak say about His statement,
h
And the grain with husks
, he said: The husks are the straw.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told us: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Dhu al-‘Asf He said:
m: al-‘Asf is the crop.

x: Some of them said: Al-Asf is the grain of wheat and barley itself.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And the grain with husks and basil
, as for the husks: it is wheat and barley. As for his saying, and basil, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: It is sustenance.

c: Zayd ibn Akhzam al-Ta’i told me: Aamer ibn Mudrik told us: Utbah ibn Yaqzan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Every basil mentioned in the Qur’an is provision.

c: Muhammad bin Omar told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And basil means sustenance.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And basil means sustenance.

x: Some of them say: Our basil.

c: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And basil means the wind.

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Yunus bin Muhammad told us: Abdul Wahid told us: Abu Rawq Atiyah bin Al-Harith told us:
m: I heard Al-Dahhak say about His statement, And basil, he said: Provisions and food.

x: Others said: It is the smelly basil.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Rayhan is what the earth produces from basil.
b.via: his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And basil,: And whatever the earth produces of basil.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And basil, he said: This is your basil.

c: And the grain having husks and the basil Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, and basil, that it refers to the herbs whose scent is found.

x: Others said: It is the greenery of the crops.

c: Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, and basil, meaning the greenery of the crops.

x: Others said: It is what stands on a leg.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaafar, on the authority of Saeed, he said:
m: Basil is what grows on a stalk. The most correct of the sayings is the one that says: What is meant by it is sustenance, which is the grain that is eaten. We said that this is the most correct of the sayings about it, because God, the Most High, the Most Praised, informed us about the seed that it has the husk, and that is what we described of the leaves that come from it and the straw when it dries. So what is more appropriate for basil is that its seed is the one that grows it, since it is from the same type as the husk, and it is heard from the Arabs who say: We went out seeking God’s basil and His provision. And it is said: Glory be to You and Your basil, meaning and Your provision. And from this is the saying of Al-Nimr ibn Talib: God's peace, his basil, his paradise, and his sky of pearls It was mentioned that some of them used to say: Asf is the edible grain, and Basil is the healthy one that has not been eaten. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement, and basil. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, some of the Meccans, and some of the Kufians read it in the nominative case, in apposition to al-hubb, meaning: and in it is the husk-bearing seed, and in it is basil as well. The majority of the Kufians recited and basil in the accusative case, in apposition to al-‘asf, meaning: and the husk-bearing seed and basil. The first of the two readings is more correct: a reading in the accusative case for the reason explained in its interpretation, and that it means sustenance. As for those who read it in the nominative case, they directed its interpretation, in my opinion, to it being the fragrant basil, and for that reason they chose the nominative case for it. And its being in the accusative case with the meaning: And in it is the grain with leaves and straw and the edible sustenance is more appropriate and better for what we explained before.

The majority of the reciters of Basra and Medina, and some of the Kufians, read it as al-Munsha’at with a fatha on the sheen, meaning the raised ones, the fortresses that come and go.

x: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny

? God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord, O company of jinn and mankind, which He bestowed upon you by sending the ships floating in the sea, flowing with your benefits, would you deny?

God Almighty says: Everyone on the face of the earth, whether jinn or human, will perish, but the Face of your Lord, O Muhammad, will remain, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Possessor of Majesty and Honor is an attribute of the Face, so He raised the word Possessor. It was mentioned in Abdullah’s reading with the letter ya “Possessor of Majesty and Honor” as an attribute and description of the Lord.
And the Face of your Lord, full of majesty and honor, will remain.

x: Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny

? God Almighty says: Then which of the favors of your Lord, O group of jinn and mankind, which He has bestowed upon you, by directing you to what is in your best interests and by what He knows better than you, by turning you over to what is most beneficial for you, would you deny?
The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement,
, O two heavy things. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Meccans, recited it as
with a nun. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it as

with a ya and a fat-ha, in response to His statement, He who is in the heavens and the earth asks Him. He did not say, He who is in the heavens asks Us. So follow the good, scholar. The correct thing to say about this, in our view, is that they are two well-known readings with similar meanings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct. As for its interpretation: It is a threat and warning from God to His servants, like the saying of the speaker who threatens and warns others, but has no business to distract him from His punishment: I will devote myself to you, and I will devote myself to you, and I will devote myself to you, meaning: I will strive to deal with your matter and punish you.

And the speaker who has no business may say: You have devoted yourself to me, and you have devoted yourself to cursing me, meaning you have taken up and turned to it. And likewise His statement, may His praise be exalted, We will devote ourselves to you, we will hold you to account and take action in your matter, O mankind and jinn, so we will punish the people of disobedience and reward the people of obedience. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

God Almighty says: And in these two gardens of abundant rain are fruits, palm trees, and pomegranates. There is a difference of opinion about the meaning for which the date palm and pomegranate were mentioned again. It was previously mentioned that they contain fruit.
Some of them said: It was repeated because the date palm and pomegranate are not fruits.

Others said: They are from the fruit. They said: We said they are from the fruit because the Arabs consider them from the fruit. They said: If we are asked: How are they repeated when they have been mentioned with the rest of the fruit? We say: That is Guard strictly the prayers and the middle prayer Al-Baqarah 2:238. He commanded them to guard every prayer. Then He repeated the afternoon prayer to emphasize it. Likewise, the palm trees and pomegranates were repeated to encourage the people of Paradise. He said: That is like His statement: Do you not see that to God prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth? Al-Hajj 22:18. Then He said: And many of the people, and many upon whom the punishment has become just Al-Hajj 22:18. He mentioned them at the beginning of the statement in His statement: whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth Al-Hajj 22:18.

Their branches are of gold, their clusters are of gold, their clusters are of gold, and their dates are like jugs, whiter than milk and silver, sweeter than honey and sugar, and softer than butter and ghee.

Then which of the favors of your Lord would you deny

m: And the genius of Hassan, said Zarabi.

c: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us:
m: Ibn Zayd said on the authority of Qatada: And two beautiful ones. He said: The two beautiful ones are the carpets.

x: Others said: The genius is brocade.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And Abqari
h
Reclining on green cushions

and fine carpets Hassan, he said: It is brocade. The reciters in all countries read that as On a green rug and Abqari Hassan without an alif in both letters. A report was mentioned from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, which is not preserved and whose chain of transmission is not authentic: On a green rug and Abqari with an alif and the procedure. It was mentioned from Zuhair al-Farqabi that he used to read On a green rug with an alif and left out the procedure and Abqari Hassan with an alif also and without the procedure. As for the rugs in this reading, it may be possible to find the correct form, but as for Abqari, there is no way for it to be correct according to the people of Arabic, because the alif of the group is not followed by four letters or three correct letters. As for the first reading that was mentioned from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, if it were correct, then the two words would have to be unconventional.

notes.en: al-Ṭaḥāwī transmitted it in al-Mushkil 10:160 after report (3993), and Abū Nuʿaym in al-Ḥilya 3:281 through Jarīr. Ibn Abī Shayba 13:570 and Ḥannād in al-Zuhd (899) transmitted it through Manṣūr. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:146 to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr, ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in al-Tawba, and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه الطحاوي في المشكل 10/ 160 عقب ح (3993)، وأبو نعيم في الحلية 3/ 281 من طريق جرير به، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة 13/ 570، وهناد في الزهد (899) من طريق منصور به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 146 إلى سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن أبي الدنيا في التوبة وابن المنذر.

notes.en: The base text reads: “she feared it.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "خافته".

notes.en: Ibn Abī Shayba in his Tafsīr, Aḥmad ibn Manīʿ, Abū Yaʿlā—as cited in al-Maṭālib (4130, 4131)—and al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-kabīr 4:296 transmitted it through al-Jurayrī. al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (11561) and Ibn Khuzayma in al-Tawḥīd, p. 223, transmitted it through Muḥammad ibn Saʿd.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة في تفسيره، وأحمد بن منيع، وأبو يعلى - كما في المطالب (4130، 4131) - والبخاري في التاريخ الكبير 4/ 296 من طريق الجريري به، والنسائي في الكبرى (11561)، وابن خزيمة في التوحيد ص 223 من طريق محمد بن سعد به.

notes.en: Ṣ and M add after it: “even if he committed fornication or theft.”
notes.ar: بعده في ص، م: "زنى وإن سرق".

notes.en: Ibn Mardawayh—as cited in al-Taghlīq 5:167—and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth (30) transmitted it through Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam. Aḥmad 14:311 (8683), al-Nasāʾī in al-Kubrā (11560), al-Ṭaḥāwī in Sharḥ al-mushkil (3993), and al-Baghawī in his Tafsīr 7:451–452 transmitted it through Muḥammad ibn Abī Ḥarmala. al-Bukhārī in al-Tārīkh al-kabīr 4:297, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and al-Ṭabarānī—as cited in Fatḥ al-Bārī 11:267—transmitted it through ʿAṭāʾ. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:146 to al-Ḥakīm in Nawādir al-uṣūl and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن مردويه - كما في التغليق 5/ 167 - والبيهقي في البعث (30) من طريق سعيد بن أبي مريم به، وأخرجه أحمد 14/ 311 (8683)، والنسائي في الكبرى (11560)، والطحاوي في شرح المشكل (3993)، والبغوي في تفسيره 7/ 451، 452 من طريق محمد بن أبي حرملة به، وأخرجه البخاري في التاريخ الكبير 4/ 297، وابن أبي حاتم، والطبراني - كما في الفتح 11/ 267 - من طريق عطاء به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 146 إلى الحكيم في نوادر الأصول وابن المنذر.

notes.en: M reads: “from.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 33:144.

notes.en: al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Baʿth wa-l-nushūr (242) through Muʾammal. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:146 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في البعث والنشور (242) من طريق مؤمل به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 146 إلى ابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: The base text reads: “Sinān.” See Tahdhīb al-kamāl 12:6.
notes.ar: في الأصل: "سنان". وينظر تهذيب الكمال 12/ 6.

notes.en: Ibn al-Mubārak transmitted it in al-Zuhd (924), and Ibn Ḥibbān in al-Thiqāt 4:335, through Muʿtamir. al-Bazzār—as cited in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:146—and through him Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in al-Tamhīd 9:241–242 transmitted it through Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abū al-Dardāʾ. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:146 to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن المبارك في الزهد (924)، وابن حبان في الثقات 4/ 335 من طريق معتمر به، وأخرجه البزار - كما في الدر المنثور 6/ 46، ومن طريقه ابن في التمهيد 9/ 241، 242 - من طريق زيد بن وهب، عن أبي الدرداء، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 146 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: The base text reads: “Ḥārith.” Cited above, 2:84, 86, and 88.
notes.ar: في الأصل: "حارث". وتقدم في 2/ 84، 86، 88.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 7:477—transmitted it through ʿAbd al-Salām ibn Ḥarb. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147 to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 7/ 477 - من طريق عبد السلام بن حرب به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 147 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.en: This is Thābit ibn Kaʿb, nicknamed Quṭna. The two verses and a third appear in al-Aghānī 14:262; the first verse appears in Lisān al-ʿArab, root h-d-l.
notes.ar: هو ثابت بن كعب الملقب بقطنة، والبيتان مع ثالث في الأغاني 14/ 262، والبيت الأول في اللسان (هـ د ل).

notes.en: The base text, Ṣ, T1, and T3 read: “cooing”; al-Aghānī reads: “weeping.” Hadhīl is the sound of doves. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root h-d-l.
notes.ar: في الأصل، ص، ت 1، ت 3: "هدير"، وفي الأغاني: "بكاء". والهديل: صوت الحمام. اللسان (هـ د ل).

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in Ibn Kathīr’s Tafsīr 7:477—transmitted it through Abū Qutayba. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abī Bakr ibn Ḥibbān in al-Funūn, and Ibn al-Anbārī in al-Waqf wa-l-ibtidāʾ.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره - كما في تفسير ابن كثير 7/ 477 - من طريق أبي قتيبة به، عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 147 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وأبي بكر بن حبان في الفنون وابن الأنباري في الوقف والابتداء.

notes.en: M reads: “the fruit.” Ḥannād transmitted the report in al-Zuhd (43) through Abū Sinān, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
notes.ar: في م: "الفاكهة". والأثر أخرجه هناد في الزهد (43) من طريق أبي سنان، عن الضحاك.

notes.en: al-Ḥāfiẓ cites it in al-Taghlīq 3:505 from the author.
notes.ar: ذكره الحافظ في التغليق 3/ 505 عن المصنف.

notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "فيما بين".

notes.en: Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and T3 read: “it sways.” Māsa yamīsu means “he pranced and strutted”; a mayyās branch is swaying. See Lisān al-ʿArab, root m-y-s.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "يمس". وماس يميس ميسًا وميسانا: تبختر واختال، وغصن مياس: مائل. اللسان (م ي س).

notes.ar: في ت 2، ت 3، ومصدر التخريج: "فصول".

notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في البعث والنشور (307) من طريق محمد بن سعد به مطولًا.

notes.en: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmitted it in his Tafsīr 2:265 through Maʿmar. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 265 عن معمر به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 147 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and T3 read: “good.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "حسن".

notes.en: This is Abū ʿUbayda in Majāz al-Qurʾān 2:245.
notes.ar: هو أبو عبيدة في مجاز القرآن 2/ 245.

notes.en: That is, “thickness.” See al-Muʿjam al-wasīṭ, root ṣ-f-q.
notes.ar: أي كثافة. ينظر الوسيط (ص ف ق).

notes.en: Ṣ, M, T1, T2, and T3 read: “al-ʿarqa.” Firind is a type of silk. See al-Jawālīqī, al-Muʿarrab, p. 291, and Tāj al-ʿarūs, root f-r-n-d.
notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "العرقة". والفرند: نوع من الحرير. ينظر المعرب للجواليقي ص 291، والتاج (فرند).

notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3: "بن".

notes.en: al-Ḥusayn al-Marwazī transmitted it in his additions to Ibn al-Mubārak’s al-Zuhd (1534); Ibn Abī Shayba 13:137 transmitted it from Yaḥyā.
notes.ar: أخرجه الحسين المروزي في زوائده على الزهد لابن المبارك (1534)، وابن أبي شيبة 13/ 137 عن يحيى به.

notes.en: Ṣ and T1 read: “Barīm”; T2 and T3 read: “Maryam.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1: "بريم"، وفي ت 2، ت 3: "مريم".

notes.en: al-Firyābī—as cited in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147—and through him Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in Ṣifat al-janna (158) transmitted it. al-Ḥākim 2:475 and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth wa-l-nushūr (339) transmitted it through Sufyān al-Thawrī. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad, Ibn Abī Ḥātim, and Ibn Mardawayh.
notes.ar: أخرجه الفريابي - كما في الدر المنثور 6/ 147 - ومن طريقه ابن أبي الدنيا في صفة الجنة (158)، وأخرجه الحاكم 2/ 475، والبيهقي في البعث والنشور (339) من طريق سفيان الثوري به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور إلى عبد بن حميد وعبد الله بن أحمد وابن أبي حاتم وابن مردويه.

notes.en: al-Baghawī mentions it in his Tafsīr 7:453; al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr 17:179.
notes.ar: ذكره البغوي في تفسيره 7/ 453، والقرطبي في تفسيره 17/ 179.

notes.ar: هو الفراء في معاني القرآن 3/ 118.

notes.ar: في م، ت 2، ت 3: "شرك".

notes.en: al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147 to the author and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.

notes.en: Ibn Abī Ḥātim—as cited in al-Itqān 2:47—and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth (308) transmitted a similar report through Abū Ṣāliḥ. al-Suyūṭī attributes an extended version in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم - كما في الإتقان 2/ 47 - والبيهقي في البعث (308) من طريق أبي صالح به بنحوه، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 147 مطولًا إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: The base text reads: “He honored him.”
notes.ar: في الأصل: "أكرمه".

notes.ar: سقط من: ص، م، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3.

notes.en: Ḥannād in al-Zuhd (17), Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in Ṣifat al-janna (329), and al-Bayhaqī in al-Baʿth wa-l-nushūr (388) transmitted a similar report through Manṣūr, from Mujāhid. al-Firyābī—as cited in al-Taghlīq 4:334—transmitted it through Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147 to Ibn Abī Shayba and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه هناد في الزهد (17)، وابن أبي الدنيا في صفة الجنة (329)، والبيهقي في البعث والنشور (388) من طريق منصور عن مجاهد بنحوه. وأخرجه الفريابي - كما في التغليق 4/ 334 - من طريق ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد به، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 147 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: al-Bayhaqī transmitted it in al-Baʿth wa-l-nushūr (392) through Saʿīd. Ibn al-Qayyim attributed it in Ḥādī al-arwāḥ, p. 169, to Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr in his Tafsīr. al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:147 to ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه البيهقي في البعث والنشور (392) من طريق سعيد به، وعزاه ابن القيم في حادي الأرواح ص 169 إلى سعيد بن منصور في تفسيره، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 147 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: al-Baghawī mentions it in his Tafsīr 7:453; Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr 7:479.
notes.ar: ذكره البغوي في تفسيره 7/ 453، وابن كثير في تفسيره 7/ 479.

notes.en: The base text adds after it: “before them, neither jinn.”
notes.ar: بعده في الأصل: "قبلهم ولا جان".

notes.ar: في ص، ت 2، ت 3: "مشطه حبل قط".

notes.en: This is al-Farrāʾ in Maʿānī al-Qurʾān 3:119. See Tahdhīb al-lugha 13:316.
notes.ar: هو الفراء في معاني القرآن 3/ 119، وينظر تهذيب اللغة 13/ 316.

notes.en: Ṣ, T1, T2, T3, and al-Zuhd read “Sulaym.” In the preceding passage, al-Bukhārī says that it was Wakīʿ who said “Sulaym.” Al-Bukhārī also reports that ʿAbda said: “Sulaymān, from Jāriya.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ت 3، والزهد: "سليم". وذكر البخاري في الموضع السابق أن الذي قال: سليم. إنما هو وكيع. وقال البخاري: وقال عبدة: سليمان، عن جارية.

notes.ar: في ص، م، ت 1، ت 2: "السلمي". وينظر الأنساب 5/ 297.

notes.en: We have established the wording here in this form because the author says of this chain: “Thus he said.”
notes.ar: أثبتناه في هذا الموضع هكذا؛ لقول المصنف في هذا الإسناد: هكذا قال.

notes.en: The manuscripts read “Ḥāritha.” See the note on it on the preceding page.

notes.en: al-Bukhārī transmitted it in al-Tārīkh al-kabīr 2:283 through Marwān. Ḥannād and al-Bukhārī have “Jāriya ibn Sulaym,” while Ibn Abī Shayba has “Ḥāritha ibn Sulaymān.” al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr 6:149 to al-Firyābī and ʿAbd ibn Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: أخرجه البخاري في التاريخ الكبير 2/ 283 من طريق مروان به، وأخرجه ابن أبي شيبة في مصنفه 13/ 131، وهناد في الزهد (41)، والبخاري في الموضع السابق عن وكيع - زاد ابن أبي شيبة: وعبدة -، عن إسماعيل به، وعند هناد والبخاري: جارية بن سليم، وعند ابن أبي شيبة: حارثة بن سليمان. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 149 إلى الفريابي وعبد بن حميد.

notes.en: ʿArājīn is the plural of ʿurjūn, the stalk bearing dates. See al-Wasīṭ, root ʿ-r-j-n.

notes.en: Thafārīq is the plural of thufruq, a division of a date-cluster branch. See al-Nihāya 1:215.
notes.ar: الثفاريق جمع تفروق، وهو شعبة من شمراخ العذق. النهاية 1/ 215.
